evidence.excerpt:
General-purpose benchmarks test information reten-
tion, updating, and access; domain-specific bench-
marks must further establish whether these capabilities
meet specialized operational requirements. To make
this additional coverage explicit, our three-dimensional
Scenario–Challenge–Capability (SCC) design method
translatesrequirementsinadequatelycoveredbygeneral
tests into representative tasks. Associations across the
three dimensions allow designers to inspect how these
tasks complement general evaluation.
The challenge dimension identifies memory require-
ments that need particular attention: domain-specific
issues and common issues subject to stronger con-
straints or more serious consequences in that domain.
Benchmark designers should identify these difficul-
ties as fully as possible and specify what history each
challenge requires, when the agent needs it, and what
happens if it

The 140 templates yield 2240 instances across nine
scenario tasks: 840 easy, 840 medium, and 560 hard.
Table 3 summarizes their distribution by task.
A specified random strategy without history access
earnsfullscoresonanaverageof1.07ofthe16instances
per template. The template-average probability of full
scores on at least 8 instances is 0.0229% (Table 4).
Random choices thus rarely yield full scores across
multiple instances, showing how evaluation across a
template's instances limits the influence of chance suc-
cesses. AppendixCgivesthestrategyandcalculations.

checks verify consistency between evidence, execution
rules, and scores. Offline programs reconstruct rules
and states from public text in the frozen test set; for

evidence.excerpt:
For each test, we initialize an independent workspace
and memory store. After ingesting 30 read-only histor-
ical turns sequentially, the agent executes the current
task through environment tools, using actual feedback
to guide subsequent actions. Scoring uses the first
scored terminal state. Between instances, we clear
workspaces, skills, and storage to keep histories and
memories independent. If infrastructure interrupts a
test, the interruption is recorded separately and execu-
tion resumes using the same evaluation unit.
Same-session evaluation (same_session) runs the
current task in the history-ingestion session. New-
session evaluation (new_session) starts through the
nativeinterface,retainingtheinstance'spersistentmem-
ory. The former permits continued use of raw interac-
tioncontext;thelattertestswhetherestablishedmemory
supports task continuation.
Clean and background histories

missing_information: Dataset quality controls, licensing, ethics, or documentation were not detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluated systems were frozen and run against the benchmark without tuning or training against its score, so no optimization loop is present.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic rule-based environment scoring of task completion, state changes, safety conditions, and resource use.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the benchmark evaluates off-the-shelf and baseline configurations without adapting them against the benchmark's score.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the relative merits of persistent memory systems, cross-session retention gaps, and differing trade-offs between static fact retrieval and dynamic state tracking are well supported by the experimental results and paired ablations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is thorough, executing 26,880 main experiment runs and 20,160 paired ablation runs across six system configurations, complete with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, token efficiency metrics, and random-chance baselines.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluated systems were frozen and tested directly without optimization against the evaluation metric.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic environment scoring function assessing state transitions, task completion, safety violations, and resource expenditure.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable; the benchmark evaluates off-the-shelf and baseline agent configurations (Pi Agent, RAG, Mem0, CoM, LightMem, SpaceMind) without tuning or training them against the benchmark's score.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report limitations, including focus on discrete turn histories rather than continuous real-time execution, specific simulation constraints, and potential bias favoring static fact retention over dynamic procedural execution.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology systematically operationalizes operational challenges into 140 templates across 9 scenario tasks with deterministic environment state transitions, isolated session management, and deterministic rule-based scoring based on task completion, state updates, safety constraints, and resource consumption.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper makes an extensive, rigorously validated contribution to evaluating embodied agent memory in domain-specific constraints with deterministic programmatic grading, controlled ablations, and clear reporting of statistical uncertainty.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces AstroMemBench, a comprehensive benchmark and Scenario-Challenge-Capability design framework for evaluating long-term memory systems in embodied spacecraft agents across 16 subchallenges and 2,240 test instances.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper makes an extensive, rigorously validated contribution to evaluating embodied agent memory in domain-specific constraints with deterministic programmatic grading, controlled ablations, and clear reporting of statistical uncertainty.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report limitations, including focus on discrete turn histories rather than continuous real-time execution, specific simulation constraints, and potential bias favoring static fact retention over dynamic procedural execution.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
